title: The Operational Facilitator's alignment review gates whether a Root Edit proposal ever reaches a token holder vote
content:
A.6.1.1.4.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3 requires that "within seven (7) days of the proposal being submitted, the Operational Facilitator must review the Root Edit Proposal for alignment." An aligned finding is announced on the Forum post along with a confirmation "that the proposal is feasible for Operational GovOps to operationalize"; a misaligned finding must be announced too, "and provide the reasoning for it."

A.6.1.1.4.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 then makes the vote conditional on that outcome: "Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Skybase Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll."

This places a substantive check ahead of the token vote rather than after it. The token holders are not the first filter — alignment is. Formally the Facilitator is not exercising a veto over an outcome; they are declining to open a vote that could only produce an invalid one, since edits violating the Core Atlas are prohibited outright.

The safeguards on that power are procedural and reputational: a hard 7-day deadline so proposals cannot be killed by inaction, mandatory publication of the finding, and mandatory reasoning for a rejection. Note also the dual test — a proposal must be both *aligned* and *operationally feasible*, so the Facilitator screens for GovOps capacity as well as legality, which gives one role visibility into two otherwise separate constraints.

The residual tension is real: an appointed Facilitator, supplied under an Accord by a different Agent, can prevent SKYBASE holders from expressing a view at all.
